description: Third-Party/Vendor Risk Management overlay. A vendor is the 'account'; a risk analyst reads the causal evidence graph instead of a KPI health score, so this vertical ships with an empty KPI catalog (tprm_v1_kpi_catalog.json) -- signals-only, the same proven pattern as any evidence-only vertical. Every subtype below is new vocabulary mapped into the existing 17 signal roles (additive-only over taxonomy_base.json, same mechanism datacenter_v1 uses) -- no new roles, no code changes. Each reused role's polarity (backend/utils/taxonomy_loader.py's NEGATIVE_SIGNAL_ROLES/POSITIVE_SIGNAL_ROLES) is inherited automatically by whatever subtype is filed under it.

infra_incident.is: A security breach, data breach, outage, service disruption, or SLA breach at the vendor -- something that actually happened, not a risk of it happening.
infra_incident.not: A scheduled maintenance window the vendor announced in advance.

escalation.is: A vendor issue raised above normal account management: our executives get involved, a legal dispute opens, or a regulator inquires.
escalation.not: A routine support ticket or status call.

commercial_pressure.is: The vendor's financial or ownership stability is in question: distress signals, bankruptcy risk, an M&A event, a change of ownership, or a pricing dispute.
commercial_pressure.not: A price increase we've already agreed to and aren't contesting.

capacity_pressure.is: The vendor is running short of the capacity or delivery bandwidth we depend on.
capacity_pressure.not: A one-off delay the vendor has already explained and resolved.

delivery_stall.is: A remediation, onboarding step, or requested audit response from the vendor is delayed or blocked.
delivery_stall.not: A delay we caused on our own side.

champion_change.is: Our named contact or relationship owner AT THE VENDOR leaves, changes role, or is replaced.
champion_change.not: A change of contact on our own team.

product_friction.is: The vendor's product or service itself is deficient: a quality defect, a formal complaint, or an audit finding against them.
product_friction.not: A one-off user complaint the vendor already resolved -- that is recovery.

engagement_decline.is: The vendor is slower to respond or less available than before: missed reviews, slow answers to security questionnaires, unreturned outreach.
engagement_decline.not: A single late reply during a holiday period.

usage_decline.is: The scope of services we actually draw from this vendor is shrinking.
usage_decline.not: A planned, mutually agreed scope reduction with no risk implication.

recovery.is: A previously flagged vendor issue is confirmed resolved: remediation completed, an SLA restored, an incident closed out.
recovery.not: The vendor claiming it's fixed with no confirmation.

advocacy.is: The vendor is positively referenced: a strong review, a reference call offered, praise from our own stakeholders.
advocacy.not: Politeness in an otherwise neutral message.

expansion_intent.is: We are discussing expanding the vendor's scope, services, or contract value.
expansion_intent.not: An expansion that has already been signed -- that is expansion_realized.

expansion_realized.is: A vendor scope expansion or contract renewal actually closed or signed.
expansion_realized.not: A verbal agreement not yet documented.

announcement.is: The vendor states a decision already made: discontinuing a service, terminating the contract, or exiting a market.
announcement.not: A hint or rumor of the same -- that is commercial_pressure or capacity_pressure.

crm_flag.is: Our own risk team's or account owner's judgment call about this vendor, entered directly rather than derived from a vendor-side event.
crm_flag.not: Anything the vendor itself said or did.

intervention.is: An action WE took in response to vendor risk: a corrective action plan issued, a mitigation step, an escalation we initiated.
intervention.not: An action the vendor took unprompted.

routine.is: Business as usual: a scheduled review, a routine audit, an ordinary status update with no risk signal.
routine.not: A status update that discloses a new issue -- classify that under the issue's own role instead.

signal_examples.text: Vendor disclosed a data breach affecting a subset of customer records; they notified us under the incident clause 4 hours after detection.
Our primary security contact at Acme Corp left last week -- their new point of contact hasn't been introduced yet.
Acme's parent company announced a majority stake sale to a PE firm; deal expected to close next quarter.
Remediation plan for the Q2 audit finding was completed and verified by our team this week.
Quarterly business review went well, no new issues, contract renewal discussion tabled for next cycle.
